name: India
description: Subcontinental cradle of profound spiritual philosophies, mathematics (zero and decimal systems), magnificent rock-cut cave temples, grand dynastic empires, and global maritime trade.

kingdoms.title: Maurya Empire
kingdoms.description: Emperor Ashoka sent his son, Mahinda Thero, and later his daughter, Sanghamitta Theri, to Sri Lanka to introduce Buddhism.
kingdoms.biography: The Maurya Empire was a geographically extensive Iron Age historical power based in Magadha and founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Under Ashoka the Great, the empire embraced Buddhism and spread its teachings across Asia, including to Sri Lanka through his son Mahinda.

sections.heading: Connection to Sri Lanka
content: Emperor Ashoka sent his son, Mahinda Thero, and later his daughter, Sanghamitta Theri, to Sri Lanka to introduce Buddhism.
This event fundamentally transformed Sri Lankan culture, architecture, and governance.

content: Invention of the decimal system and zero by Aryabhata

content: First Battle of Panipat won by Babur in 1526
Akbar's Din-i Ilahi tolerance and administrative Mansabdari system

kings.title: Ashoka the Great
kings.biography: Ashoka was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE. He promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia.

sections.heading: Biography
content: After the brutal Kalinga War, Ashoka renounced violence and embraced Buddhism.
He established a welfare state, built hospitals for people and animals, and erected pillars with edicts promoting morality.

kings.title: Chandragupta Maurya
kings.biography: Founder of the Maurya Empire, defeating the Nanda Dynasty and Seleucus I Nicator with the guidance of Chanakya to unite northern India under a single crown.

kings.title: Emperor Ashoka the Great
kings.biography: Mauryan Emperor who embraced Buddhism following the remorse of the Kalinga War, erecting the Pillars of Ashoka and dispatching Mahinda to introduce Buddhism to Sri Lanka.

kings.title: Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar
kings.biography: Third Mughal Emperor who tripled the empire's territory across South Asia, fostered religious tolerance, patronized arts, and established effective administrative systems.

sites.name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
sites.description: One of the oldest stone structures in India commissioned by Emperor Ashoka, featuring intricate torana gateways illustrating Buddhist jatakas.

sites.name: Taj Mahal
sites.description: Peerless white Makrana marble mausoleum on the Yamuna river, an official New 7 Wonder of the World.
sites.history: Commissioned by Emperor Shah Jahan to house the remains of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal. Built over 22 years by an army of 20,000 artisans under the direction of court architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
sites.construction: Crafted from translucent white Makrana marble inlaid with 28 varieties of precious and semi-precious stones (pietra dura technique) and flanked by red sandstone mosques.
sites.architecture: Flawless bilateral symmetry, a central double dome rising 73 meters, four detached minarets angled outward, and a formal Charbagh Persian paradise garden.
sites.significance: Designated an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007 and described by Rabindranath Tagore as 'a teardrop on the cheek of eternity.'
sites.currentStatus: Standing pristine and protected as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
sites.wonderHistoricalContext: Declared an official New 7 Wonder of the World on July 7, 2007, recognized worldwide as the pinnacle of Indo-Islamic architectural symmetry and devotion.
